item.title: Cecil A. Joyner
item.description: AHOSKIE – Cecil Alvin Joyner, affectionately known as Alvin and PopPop, passed away peacefully at the age of 93 on January 20, 2026, in Ahoskie, North Carolina. Born on January 19, 1933, in Murfreesboro, North Carolina, Alvin was the beloved son of the late Cecil Ervin Joyner and Jennie Garris Joyner. item.title: Melvin L. Lashley
item.description: GARYSBURG – Melvin Leon Lashley, 55, of Garysburg died Wednesday, January 28, 2026 at his residence. Funeral services will be held at 1 p.m. on Wednesday, February 4, 2026 at T.L. Faison’s Funeral Care, Seaboard, which is handling the arrangements. Burial will follow in Lashley Family Cemetery, Garysburg.

item.title: Who keeps the water running?
item.description: Before I began working as a reporter, I did not think much of the infrastructure which holds together daily life. I turned the sink on and water came out of the faucet. I got in my car and drove around on roads and over bridges that have been in place for years. It never crossed my mind how those vital parts of everyday life were put in place, nor how they were maintained to keep going for so many years. item.title: Powerball winner claims prize
item.description: RALEIGH – The lucky lottery player who won last week’s Powerball jackpot of $209.3 million claimed the prize on Thursday at lottery headquarters in Raleigh. The player, who selected the winning numbers at a business in Roanoke Rapids, chose to remain anonymous for 90 days. Under state law, when a lottery player in North Carolina wins a prize of $50 million or more, the player can choose to keep their win anonymous for up to 90 days after claiming the prize.
